title: Range Sum of BST
prompt:
Given the `root` of a binary search tree and two integers `low` and `high`, return the sum of values of all nodes with a value in the inclusive range `[low, high]`.

The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array along with `low` and `high`; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from the array, so you only need to compute the range sum.

examples.explanation: A single-node tree whose value equals both bounds still counts, contributing its own value to the sum.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 2 * 10^4]
hints: You don't need to visit every node — the BST ordering property lets you skip entire subtrees that can't contain values in range.
If a node's value is less than low, its entire left subtree is also too small and can be skipped; if it's greater than high, its entire right subtree can be skipped.
At each node, add its value to the sum only if it falls within [low, high], then recurse into whichever children could still contain in-range values.

solution.approach: Exploit the BST property to prune subtrees that provably can't contain any value in [low, high]. At each node: if its value is below low, skip the left subtree entirely (everything there is even smaller); if above high, skip the right subtree entirely (everything there is even larger); otherwise add the node's value if it's in range and recurse into both children.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n) worst case, better with a balanced tree and a narrow range
